subproblems.title: Orthogonal projection onto V does not increase mass when T is carried by V and X by a compact set K (reuse of the accepted K-variant; Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection q := V.starProjection, and let T, X, S' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ m). Let R_T, R_X be integer multiplicity triples in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m) with R_T representing T and R_X representing X. Assume μ_{R_T}(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 (RT.measure Vᶜ = 0), and that K ⊆ ℝ^P is a compact set with μ_{R_X}(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0 (RX.measure Kᶜ = 0). Assume S'(ω) = T(ω) + R_X.action(q^#ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), where q^#ω = affinePullbackForm q 0 ω, i.e. (q^#ω)(x) = ω(0 + qx)∘Λ^m q. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m) such that R.action(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω) for every test form ω, and S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)) for every set O ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T X S' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RT RX : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), RT.Represents T → RX.Represents X → RT.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → IsCompact K → RX.measure Kᶜ = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, S' ω = T ω + RX.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m))) → ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) = T ω + X ω) ∧ ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure (V.starProjection ⁻¹' O)

Accepted proof (verbatim):
Source: step 4 of the selected node's supplied proof (projection does not increase mass: |Λ_m q ξ_S(x)| ≤ Π|qτ_i| ≤ 1 by Hadamard's inequality, hence M_{W*}(q_#S) ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(W*))), together with q_#T = T from its step 1. Here S' = T + q_#X plays the role of q_#S = q_#T + q_#X, and the representation R of T + X (= S) is built so that its action is additive on the non-compactly supported forms q^#ω.
Siblings used: int_combination (Submission.rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination), projection_invariance (Submission.idtp_fons_cs_sp_action_starProjection_eq), orient_comp (Submission.dtc_bc_lc_pf_unitOrientation_comp) and pairing_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le).
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]. For an IMRep R write M_R, θ_R, ξ_R for carrier, mult and orient, and F_R(x) := 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x) ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) (R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y)). ‖·‖ is the operator norm of a covector or a linear map, |·|_E the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm). q is an orthogonal projection, so ‖q‖ ≤ 1 (starProjection_norm_le); V is closed.
1. Action as a global integral. For every IMRep R and every m-form β, F_R(x)(β(x)) = 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x)), so R.action(β) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R ξ_R(β) dμ = ∫ F_R(x)(β(x)) dμ(x) (integral_indicator, M_R measurable). If x ↦ θ_R ξ_R(β) is μ⌞M_R-integrable, then x ↦ F_R(x)(β(x)) is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff).
2. Carriers. If C is measurable and R.measure(Cᶜ) = 0, then μ⌞M_R-a.e. x lies in C. Indeed 0 = R.measure(Cᶜ) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ Cᶜ} θ_R dμ (withDensity_apply, restrict_restrict) ≥ μ(M_R ∩ Cᶜ) because θ_R ≥ 1 on M_R; conclude with ae_restrict_iff'.
3. Projected orientation bound. For every IMRep R, for μ⌞M_R-a.e. x and every m-covector α: |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E. Proof: by the field orients, for μ⌞M_R-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_R x) Q, i.e. ξ_R(x) = ±τ_1∧⋯∧τ_m for an orthonormal basis τ of Q. The first part of orient_comp with L := q gives |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E·‖q‖^m (in Simon's terms |⟨α, Λ_m q ξ⟩| = |α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m)| ≤ |α|_E·Π_i|qτ_i|, Hadamard's inequality). Since ‖q‖ ≤ 1 and |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), ‖q‖^m ≤ 1 (pow_le_one₀) and |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E.
4. The combined triple. Apply int_combination with U = ℝ^P (open), R₁ = RT, R₂ = RX and p₁ = p₂ = 1. It gives an IMRep R with F_R = F_RT + F_RX μ-a.e.
5. Additivity. Let β be an m-form such that x ↦ θ_RT ξ_RT(β) is μ⌞M_RT-integrable and x ↦ θ_RX ξ_RX(β) is μ⌞M_RX-integrable. By steps 1 and 4, R.action(β) = ∫ F_R(β) dμ = ∫ (F_RT + F_RX)(β) dμ (integral_congr_ae) = ∫ F_RT(β) dμ + ∫ F_RX(β) dμ (integral_add, integrability from step 1) = RT.action(β) + RX.action(β).
6. Test forms; the first conclusion. Let ω be a test form. It is continuous (hence a.e. strongly measurable for every measure) with compact support C := tsupport ω, hence bounded by some B (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and ω(x) = 0 off C (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So pairing_bound (with U = ℝ^P, F := ω) shows that θ_R ξ_R(ω) is μ⌞M_R-integrable for every IMRep R in ℝ^P. Step 5 gives R.action(ω) = RT.action(ω) + RX.action(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω), since RT represents T and RX represents X.
7. Pull-backs of test forms. Fix a test form ω, let B bound ‖ω‖ and put β := q^#ω, β(x) = ω(0 + q x)∘Λ^m q. Then β is continuous (composition of ω, x ↦ q x and the continuous linear map α ↦ α∘Λ^m q) and ‖β(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω(q x)‖·‖q‖^m ≤ B (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le, ‖q‖ ≤ 1).
 General principle: let R be an IMRep, D a closed set, C a compact set with R.measure(Dᶜ) = 0 and β(x) = 0 for x ∈ D ∖ C. Then θ_R ξ_R(β) is μ⌞M_R-integrable. Indeed F := 1_D·β is a.e. strongly measurable (β is continuous and D is Borel), vanishes off C (on D ∖ C because β does, and off D by definition), and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x (B ≥ ‖β(x)‖ ≥ 0, which also covers x ∉ D where F(x) = 0), so pairing_bound gives integrability of θ_R ξ_R(F). By step 2, F = β μ⌞M_R-a.e., so θ_R ξ_R(β) is integrable (Integrable.congr).
 (a) For RX take D = C = K (compact, hence closed); the vanishing condition is empty.
 (b) For RT take D = V and C = V ∩ tsupport ω (compact). If x ∈ V ∖ tsupport ω, then q x = x and ω(q x) = ω(x) = 0, so β(x) = 0.
 Hence step 5 applies to β, and with projection_invariance (applicable because RT.measure(Vᶜ) = 0) R.action(q^#ω) = RT.action(q^#ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = RT.action(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = T(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = S'(ω).
8. Mass bound; the second conclusion. Fix O ⊆ ℝ^P. Let ω be admissible for S'.massOn O, i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω(y)|_E ≤ 1 for all y, and let β = q^#ω. By step 7, ofReal(S'(ω)) = ofReal(R.action β) ≤ ofReal(|R.action β|) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_R} |θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x))| dμ (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). For μ⌞M_R-a.e. x (step 3):
 - if q x ∈ tsupport ω, then |ξ_R(x)(β(x))| = |ξ_R(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |ω(q x)|_E ≤ 1;
 - if q x ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(q x) = 0, so β(x) = 0.
 So the integrand is at most θ_R(x)·1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)}(x), and ∫⁻_{M_R} θ_R 1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)} dμ = R.measure(q⁻¹(tsupport ω)) (lintegral_indicator and withDensity_apply; q⁻¹(tsupport ω) is closed, hence measurable) ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)), since tsupport ω ⊆ O. As S'.massOn O is the supremum of ofReal(S'(ω)) over admissible ω (sSup_le), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)). ∎

proof_key_steps: int_combination gives R with vector density F_R = F_RT + F_RX a.e., so R.action is additive on forms whose pairings with RT and RX are integrable.

Test forms and the pull-backs q^#ω are integrable against RT and RX (pairing_bound; RT lives on V where q^#ω vanishes off tsupport ω, RX lives on the compact K). Hence R represents T + X and, by projection_invariance, R.action(q^#ω) = S'(ω).
For admissible ω with tsupport ω ⊆ O, |S'(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M_R} θ_R 1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)} dH^m = μ_R(q⁻¹(tsupport ω)) ≤ μ_R(q⁻¹(O)).

subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (reuse of the accepted declaration; Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support

Accepted proof (verbatim):
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.
